newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday January 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday January 7.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi did not rule out the need for an extra budget after a larger-than-expected 1996 public sector deficit. But Prodi said a mini-budget would cut public spending rather than raise taxes (all).

* Fierce debate over the economic treatment the Italian state grants to mafia turncoats. Interior minister Giorgio Napolitano says the government should "think about some limitation to the benefits to be allowed" (all).
* Talks between metalworkers trade unions and employers association Federmeccanica, which broke down shortly before Christmas over pay rises, are expected to resume tomorrow (all).
* Incentives for the car sector, including discounts for people scrapping their old cars and buying new ones, are effective from today (all).

* U.S. group Centenary, which is said to be interested in the ailing PC division of information technology group Olivetti, reportedly found an ally in Gianmario Rossignolo, former chairman of consumer electronics company Zanussi (Sole 24 Ore).
* A wave of rises in tariffs for motorway, electricity, water and rail transportation has already begun or is expected to be announced for this year (Corriere della Sera).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
